He completed high school at Advanced Preparatory International in [[Dallas|Dallas, Texas]], where he was a top-20 player in the Class of 2016.{{cite web | url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/242155/Terrance-Ferguson-Wont-Play-At-Arizona-Will-Go-Overseas | title=Terrance Ferguson Won't Play At Arizona, Will Go Overseas | work=RealGM.com | date=June 6, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} Ferguson made separate commitments to both [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] before deciding to skip college and play overseas in 2016–17. He is a three-time gold medalist with Team USA, and in 2016, he participated in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and the [[Nike Hoop Summit]], winning the MVP award at the latter. Ferguson was selected with the 21st overall pick of the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], where he spent three seasons before being traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in December 2020. ==High school career== [[File:20160330 MCDAAG Terrance Ferguson.jpg|thumb|right|Ferguson in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Born in [[Tulsa, Oklahoma]], Ferguson moved to [[Dallas]], [[Texas]] as a youth and enrolled at [[Prime Prep Academy]]. He joined the school's basketball team and played for coach Ray Forsett. As a freshman in 2012–13, Ferguson averaged 10 points per game and helped his team to a 38–2 record, the 2013 NACA Division I Tournament title, and the 2013 National High School Invitational semifinals. He was named to the NACA All-Tournament Team and earned NACA Tournament MVP honors.{{cite web | url=http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/f/ferguson-terrance.aspx | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623013743/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/f/ferguson-terrance.aspx | url-status=dead | archive-date=June 23, 2015 | title=Terrance Ferguson – USA Basketball | work=usab.com | access-date=June 8, 2016}} In January 2015, halfway through his junior year at Prime Prep Academy, the school closed amid allegations of theft and the mishandling of funds.{{cite web | last=Mosier | first=Jeff | url=http://www.dallasnews.com/news/community-news/best-southwest/headlines/20150207-prime-prep-academy-troubles-continue-after-closing.ece | title=Prime Prep Academy troubles continue after closing | work=DallasNews.com | date=February 7, 2015 | access-date=June 22, 2016}} In September 2015, a new institution known as Advanced Preparatory International opened in place of Prime Prep. Coach Ray Forsett subsequently joined the ranks at Advanced Prep, while four players, including Ferguson, moved over from Prime Prep with Forsett to play for Advanced Prep in 2015–16.{{cite web | last=Jordan | first=Jason | url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/coach-says-new-hoops-power-api-is-not-the-new-prime-prep-trevon-duval-billy-preston-terrance-ferguson-mark-vital | title=Coach says new hoops power Advanced Prep International is not basketball factory | work=usatodayhss.com | date=September 30, 2015 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} Heading into his senior year of high school, Ferguson was ranked No. 11 overall in the Class of 2016's ESPN 100.{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings/_/class/2016/order/true | title=Recruiting Database: 2016 ESPN 100 | work=ESPN.com | access-date=May 17, 2017}} He averaged 17.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game for Advanced Prep in 2015–16, earning a trip to the [[McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web | url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/5u11kqq0vEWSF-vLySV2xQ/texas-high-school-basketball-star-terrance-ferguson-eyeing-jump-straight-to-pros.htm | title=Texas high school basketball star Terrance Ferguson eyeing jump straight to pros | work=MaxPreps.com | date=June 7, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} As a starter for the East team, he scored 10 points in a 114–107 loss to the West.{{cite web | url=http://www.mcdonaldsallamerican.com/aag/en/MediaCenter/2016/2016-game-materials/2016-Boy-Results.html | title=2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game Results | work=mcdonaldsallamerican.com | date=March 30, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016 | archive-date=November 10, 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110004954/http://www.mcdonaldsallamerican.com/aag/en/MediaCenter/2016/2016-game-materials/2016-Boy-Results.html | url-status=dead }} On April 9, 2016, he scored 21 points, all on three-pointers, to help the USA Junior National Select Team defeat the World Select Team 101–67 at the [[Moda Center]]. It was the most lopsided victory in Nike Hoop Summit history. Ferguson's seven threes broke the Nike Hoop Summit record for threes made; the previous record of six was shared by [[Xavier Henry]] (2009) and [[Casey Jacobsen]] (1999).{{cite web | last=Jordan | first=Jason | url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/terrance-fergusons-hot-hand-lifts-team-usa-to-win-at-nike-hoop-summit | title=Terrance Ferguson's hot hand lifts Team USA to win at Nike Hoop Summit | work=usatodayhss.com | date=April 9, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} He subsequently earned MVP honors.{{cite web | last=Zagoria | first=Adam | url=https://www.sny.tv/college-recruiting/news/terrance-ferguson-commits-to-arizona/171995830 | title=Terrance Ferguson Commits to Arizona | work=SNY.tv | date=April 13, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016 | archive-date=September 27, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160927190108/https://www.sny.tv/college-recruiting/news/terrance-ferguson-commits-to-arizona/171995830 | url-status=dead }} Prior to the Nike Hoop Summit, Ferguson boasted a 19–0 record with Team USA; he made it 20–0 with USA's Summit win.{{cite web | url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/02/terrance-ferguson-hopes-to-continue-success-in-nike-hoop-summit.aspx | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160224145605/http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/02/terrance-ferguson-hopes-to-continue-success-in-nike-hoop-summit.aspx | url-status=dead | archive-date=February 24, 2016 | title=Terrance Ferguson Hopes To Continue USA Success In 2016 Nike Hoop Summit | work=usab.com | date=February 22, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} On April 30, he won the [[Ballislife All-American Game]] dunk contest after performing a free throw line dunk.{{cite web | last=Guardabascio | first=Mike | url=http://www.presstelegram.com/sports/20160430/lonzo-ball-earns-mvp-honors-at-ballislife-all-american-game-in-long-beach | title=Lonzo Ball earns MVP honors at Ballislife All-American Game in Long Beach | work=PressTelegram.com | date=April 30, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} ===Recruitment=== In January 2015, coach [[Rick Pitino]] of the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|University of Louisville]] began heavily recruiting Ferguson. Other teams showing interest in him at the time were [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] and [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]].{{cite web | last=Jones | first=Steve | url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/recruiting/louisville/2015/01/12/terrance-ferguson-recruited-heavily-louisville-basketball-team/21654327/ | title=Recruit Ferguson's mom raves about U of L | work=Courier-Journal.com | date=January 12, 2015 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} In August 2015, he committed to play for [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] in 2016–17. However, he never signed a letter of intent, and when the early signing period passed in November without Ferguson signing, other schools began contacting him.{{cite web | last=Borzello | first=Jeff | url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/story/_/id/14877858 | title=Terrance Ferguson, five-star wing, decommits from Alabama | work=ESPN.com | date=March 1, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} This led to him decommitting from Alabama on March 1, 2016. On April 13, he committed to Arizona,{{cite web | last=Borzello | first=Jeff | url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/15199191 | title=Five-star wing Terrance Ferguson, No. 13 in ESPN 100, picks Arizona | work=ESPN.com | date=April 13, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} the first day of the spring signing period, but did not sign a letter of intent despite indications he would, eventually signing non-binding financial aid papers.{{cite web | last=Pascoe | first=Bruce | url=http://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/wildcat-signee-ferguson-reportedly-may-head-overseas/article_6391dfc6-2c50-11e6-86ad-a3abacaa6871.html | title=Wildcat signee Ferguson reportedly may head overseas | work=Tucson.com | date=June 7, 2016 | access-date=June 8, 2016}} His commitment to Arizona lasted until early June, when rumors emerged that Ferguson had decided to skip college for a chance to play overseas in 2016–17. On June 6, Australia was deemed the most likely destination, with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] rumored to be close to formalizing a deal with Ferguson.{{cite web |last=Nagy |first=Boti |date=June 7, 2016 |title=Adelaide 36ers move on US high school star Terrance Ferguson to run with new Lithuanian champion Jerome Randle |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/basketball/adelaide-36ers-move-on-us-high-school-star-terrance-ferguson-to-run-with-new-lithuanian-champion-jerome-randle/news-story/28cc93c456554b198bad5a40044527e2 |access-date=June 3, 2023 |work=AdelaideNow.com.au}} By the end of the month, he had informed Wildcats coach Sean Miller of his decision to pursue professional opportunities instead of attending Arizona.{{cite web | last=Norlander | first=Matt | url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/five-star-commit-terrance-ferguson-is-leaving-arizona-to-play-overseas/ | title=Five-star commit Terrance Ferguson is leaving Arizona to play overseas | work=CBSSports.com | date=June 30, 2016 | access-date=June 30, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Adelaide 36ers (2016–2017)=== On July 1, 2016, Ferguson signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] for the [[2016–17 NBL season]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nbl.com.au/adelaide-36ers/adelaide-announce-terrance-ferguson/ | title=ADELAIDE SIGN US TEEN STAR TERRANCE FERGUSON | work=NBL.com.au | date=July 1, 2016 | access-date=July 1, 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704184647/http://www.nbl.com.au/adelaide-36ers/adelaide-announce-terrance-ferguson/ | archive-date=July 4, 2016 }}{{cite web |last=Uluc |first=Olgun |date=July 1, 2016 |title=Adelaide 36ers sign star US high-schooler Terrance Ferguson |url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/more-sports/adelaide-36ers-sign-star-us-highschooler-terrance-ferguson/news-story/663d98b402545a6e1b77a4b5bfc3ca26 |access-date=July 1, 2016 |work=heraldsun.com.au}} On October 7, 2016, he made his debut for the 36ers in their season opener against the [[Illawarra Hawks]]. In 17½ minutes off the bench, he scored 10 points on 4-of-9 shooting in a 122–88 loss.{{cite web | url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/irresistible-hawks-crush-sixers-set-scoring-record/ | title=IRRESISTIBLE HAWKS CRUSH SIXERS, SET SCORING RECORD | work=NBL.com.au | date=October 7, 2016 | access-date=October 7, 2016 | archive-date=February 9, 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209123034/https://nbl.com.au/featured-news/irresistible-hawks-crush-sixers-set-scoring-record/ | url-status=dead }} On October 14, 2016, he scored 13 points in a 98–87 loss to [[Melbourne United]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nbl.com.au/adelaide-36ers/melbourne-holds-off-sixers-first-win/ | title=MELBOURNE HOLDS OFF SIXERS FOR FIRST WIN | work=NBL.com | date=October 14, 2016 | access-date=October 14, 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018221512/http://www.nbl.com.au/adelaide-36ers/melbourne-holds-off-sixers-first-win/ | archive-date=October 18, 2016 }} On October 24, 2016, he was handed a two-game suspension for striking following the 36ers' Round 3 game against the [[Cairns Taipans]] on October 21. The incident occurred during the first quarter and involved Taipans' player [[Mark Worthington]].{{cite web |last=Nagy |first=Boti |date=October 25, 2016 |title=Adelaide 36ers consider appeal as NBL bans young import Terrance Ferguson two games for 'striking' |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/basketball/adelaide-36ers-consider-appeal-as-nbl-bans-young-import-terrance-ferguson-two-games-for-striking/news-story/1d322fe85d2ea4ae1216e778dd205cad |access-date=June 3, 2023 |work=AdelaideNow.com.au}} By accepting the charge via an early guilty plea, only a one-game suspension was imposed.{{cite web | url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/round-3-game-review-panel-rulings/ | title=ROUND 3 GAME REVIEW PANEL RULINGS | work=NBL.com.au | date=October 26, 2016 | access-date=November 30, 2016}} On January 19, 2017, he tied his season high with 13 points in a 101–68 win over the [[Brisbane Bullets]].{{cite web | url=http://www.fibalivestats.com/u/NBL/314688/bs.html | title=36ers vs Bullets | work=FIBALiveStats.com.au | date=January 19, 2017 | access-date=January 19, 2017}} The 36ers finished the regular season in first place with a 17–11 record, but were knocked out in the semi-finals by the fourth-seeded Illawarra Hawks, losing the best-of-three series 2–1. Ferguson appeared in 30 of the team's 31 games in 2016–17, averaging 4.6 points and 1.2 rebounds in 15.2 minutes per game. Following the conclusion of the season, he returned to the U.S. to begin preparations for the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Nagy |first=Boti |date=March 1, 2017 |title=Sacre bleu! Jerome off to France but 36ers plan multi-year deal for NBL's reigning MVP |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/basketball/sacre-bleu-jerome-off-to-france-but-36ers-plan-multiyear-deal-for-nbls-reigning-mvp/news-story/58edb7a7be418d8e600c50d14fff6251 |access-date=June 3, 2023 |work=AdelaideNow.com.au}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2017–2020)=== On June 22, 2017, Ferguson was selected by his hometown team, the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], with the 21st overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite web |date=June 22, 2017 |title=Thunder Selects Terrance Ferguson in 2017 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/draft-ferguson-170623 |access-date=June 22, 2017 |work=NBA.com}}{{cite web |last=Gallo |first=Nick |date=June 22, 2017 |title=Thunder Adds Athleticism and Shooting, Selects Terrance Ferguson |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/draft/recap-170622 |access-date=June 22, 2017 |work=NBA.com}} On July 29, 2017, he signed a 4-year, $10.3 million rookie-scale contract with the Thunder.{{cite web |date=July 29, 2017 |title=Thunder Signs Terrance Ferguson |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder-signs-ferguson-170729 |access-date=July 29, 2017 |work=NBA.com}} On November 14, 2017, he was assigned to the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |date=November 14, 2017 |title=Terrance Ferguson Assigned to Oklahoma City Blue |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/ferguson-assigned-171114 |access-date=November 16, 2017 |work=NBA.com}} He was recalled the next day.{{cite web |date=November 15, 2017 |title=Terrance Ferguson Recalled From Oklahoma City Blue |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/ferguson-recalled-171115 |access-date=November 16, 2017 |work=NBA.com}} On January 3, 2018, in his first career start, Ferguson scored a career-high 24 points in a 133–96 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975311|title=Westbrook, Thunder roll to 133–96 win over skidding Lakers|work=ESPN.com|date=January 3, 2018|access-date=January 3, 2018}} On October 29, 2018, the Thunder exercised Ferguson's $2.5 million team option for the [[2019–20 Oklahoma City Thunder season|2019–20 season]].{{Cite web |title=Thunder Exercises Option on Terrance Ferguson |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/ferguson-181029 |access-date=March 2, 2022 |website=NBA}}{{Cite web |title=Terrance Ferguson Contract, Salary Cap Details & Breakdowns |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nba/new-york-knicks/terrance-ferguson-23616/transactions/ |access-date=March 2, 2022 |website=Spotrac}} On October 18, 2019, the Thunder exercised Ferguson's $3.9 million team option for the [[2020–21 Oklahoma City Thunder season|2020–21 season]].{{Cite web |title=Thunder Exercise Options on Terrence Ferguson And Shai Gilgeous-Alexander |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/nba/thunder/news/thunder-exercise-rookie-options-and-terrance-ferguson-and-shai-gilgeous-alexander |access-date=March 2, 2022 |website=Sports Illustrated}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2021)=== On December 8, 2020, Ferguson, along with [[Danny Green (basketball)|Danny Green]] and [[Vincent Poirier]], were traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Al Horford]], the draft rights to [[Théo Maledon]] and [[Vasilije Micić]], and a 2025 protected first-round pick.{{cite web |title=Team Acquires Green, Ferguson, and Poirier |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-acquires-green-ferguson-and-poirier |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 8, 2020 |date=December 8, 2020}} On March 25, 2021, Ferguson was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in a three-way trade involving the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]{{Cite web |date=March 25, 2021 |title=76ers Acquire George Hill, Ignas Brazdeikis in Three-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-acquire-george-hill-ignas-brazdeikis-three-team-trade |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} and was waived four days later.{{cite web|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks have waived Terrance Ferguson and Vincent Poirier.|url=https://twitter.com/NY_KnicksPR/status/1376537851706404864|access-date=March 29, 2021|date=March 29, 2021|website=Twitter.com}} ===Lavrio (2021–2022)=== On December 14, 2021, Ferguson signed with his first European club, [[G.S. Lavrio B.C.|Lavrio]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]], after having been in preliminary talks with other Greek teams, such as [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] and [[Ionikos Nikaias B.C.|Ionikos Nikaias]], since the beginning of the 2021–22 season.{{cite web|first=Antigoni|last=Zachari|title=Lavrio signs Terrance Ferguson|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1282568/lavrio-signs-terrance-ferguson/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=December 14, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}} Less than a month later, on January 10, 2022, he parted ways with the Greek club in order to return to the U.S., signing an [[NBA G League]] contract. In three [[Greek Basket League]] games, he averaged 2 points and 1 rebound per contest, shooting with 25% from the field and 20% from beyond the three-point arc. === Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2022) === On January 11, 2022, Ferguson was acquired via waivers by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 11, 2022|access-date=January 11, 2022}} He was released by the team on January 24, but was re-acquired on February 3.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 24, 2022|access-date=January 29, 2022}} ===GTK Gliwice (2022–2023)=== On August 27, 2022, he has signed with [[GTK Gliwice]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]] (PLK).{{Cite web|url=https://plk.pl/aktualnosci/n/22476/ferguson-wzmacnia-gtk.html|title=Ferguson wzmacnia GTK|last=|first=|date=August 27, 2022|website=plk.pl|publisher=|language=pl|access-date=August 27, 2022|archive-date=August 28, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220828215446/https://plk.pl/aktualnosci/n/22476/ferguson-wzmacnia-gtk.html|url-status=dead}} === Cape Town Tigers (2023–2024) === In September 2023, the South African club [[Cape Town Tigers]] announced they had signed Ferguson on their [[Instagram]] account.{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Cxs2VwFudaG/ |access-date=2023-10-24 |website=www.instagram.com}} He made his Tigers debut on November 21, 2023, with 11 points in a 76–61 win over [[Dynamo BBC|Dynamo]] in the [[Road to BAL]].{{Cite web |title=Cape Town Tigers v Dynamo boxscore - Africa Champions Clubs ROAD TO B.A.L. 2024 2023 - 21 November |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/africaleague/2024/qualifiers/game/1411/Cape-Town-Tigers-Dynamo |access-date=2023-11-23 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} === Bashkimi (2024) === In February 2024, the Kosovan club [[KB Bashkimi|Bashkimi]] of the [[Kosovo Basketball Superleague|Kosovo Superleague]] announced they had signed Ferguson. He parted ways with Bashkimi after just one league game in March 2024.{{Cite news|title=Erdhi me bujë të madhe, Bashkimi njofton ndarjen me Terrance Ferguson|url=https://gazetablic.com/erdhi-me-buje-te-madhe-bashkimi-njofton-ndarjen-me-terrance-ferguson/|website=gazetablic.com|language=sq}} ==National team career== Ferguson was a member of the USA Basketball Men's U16 National Team that posted a 5–0 record en route to winning gold at the 2013 [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]] in [[Maldonado, Uruguay|Maldonado]], Uruguay. He played in all five games and averaged 5.8 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game. The following year, he was a member of the USA U17 World Championship Team that posted a 7–0 record and captured the [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] gold medal in [[Dubai]]. Ferguson played in all seven games (with four starts) and averaged 9.0 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game. In July 2015, Ferguson won his third gold medal in as many years after helping Team USA go 7–0 at the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece. He played in all seven games and averaged 6.1 points, 1.6 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game. ==Personal life== Ferguson is the son of Rachelle Holdman.
